item.title: A $295 million Malibu mansion by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Tadao Ando was quietly on the market when Kanye West came unannounced
item.description: Kanye West made an unplanned visit to a stunning Malibu mansion crafted by Tadao Ando, spending four days there. He secured a stay without prior arrangement, likening his presence to that of Elvis Presley. Meanwhile, the estate was later sold to Jay-Z and Beyoncé, breaking sales records. West's personal Ando-designed property, however, is grappling with legal and financial troubles, leaving its future uncertain due to ongoing foreclosure issues. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Sinkholes, scarred land and scapegoats: the scourge of illegal gold mining in Johannesburg
item.description: There is no end in sight for the drivers of illegal mining, while police action appears ineffective Cora Bailey has been encountering illegal miners ever since she first started treating injured animals in the townships around Roodepoort, west of Johannesburg, in 1991. But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area. In late September, dozens of zama zamas – the name given to illegal miners in South Africa, meaning roughly “to take a chance” in Zulu – arrived to dig for gold across the dirt road from her charity, Claw (Community Led… Publicado también por: The Guardian - Environment. Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Sudanese diaspora and human rights groups denounce UAE nominee for UN top job
item.description: Critics cite Lana Nusseibeh’s denial of accusations the UAE is fuelling Sudan war by supporting paramilitary RSF Members of the Sudanese diaspora and international human rights monitors have denounced the candidature of an Emirati diplomat for the top job at the UN, citing her denial of accusations that the United Arab Emirates is fuelling the war in Sudan by supporting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. The UAE nominated Lana Nusseibeh last week to replace the UN secretary general, António Guterres, as he finishes his second five-year term ⁠this year, upending a race that had become… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Cleopatra’s eye makeup secret? Ancient Egyptians used lead-based kohl
item.description: In ancient Egypt, kohl was more than just a cosmetic; it served dual purposes, enhancing beauty while protecting the eyes. Studies indicate that its ingredients could boost immune responses, making it a valuable tool for health. Both men and women embraced the use of black and green powders, and ancient texts highlight the fusion of cosmetics with medicine, revealing the intricate beliefs surrounding beauty and wellness in that era. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Putin califica de "exitosa" la tercera edición de la cumbre entre Rusia y África
item.description: Terminó la tercera cumbre entre Rusia y África y el presidente Vladimir Putin calificó el encuentro, en el que se reunió con 21 líderes africanos, como "exitoso". El evento busca impulsar la cooperación de Moscú con el continente, pero también se percibe como una demostración de fuerza. Más allá de la diplomacia, Putin avanza sus planes en los países africanos, en los que busca acceso a los recursos mineros y desarrollar nuevos sistemas comerciales para evitar las sanciones occidentales por la guerra en Ucrania. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: To help farmers in Southern Africa, scientists predict when to plant native nuts
item.description: Scientists studying indigenous crops recently completed a study to advise farmers on the best time to plant bambara groundnuts, a neglected African crop. Such underutilized native plants have the potential to diversify crop production and improve food security in Southern Africa. Scientists used 50 years of climate and soil data to simulate 49 growing seasons. […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Tunisians drawn into Russia's war in Ukraine

item.title: Hay quien dice que crujirse los nudillos provoca artritis. Un médico pasó 50 años haciéndolo para demostrar qué hay de cierto
item.description: Es bastante común que, cuando una persona comienza a crujirse los nudillos, aparezca alguien que apunte a que hacer eso es malísimo para los huesos, puesto que puede acelerar la aparición de artritis. Pero esta típica frase de madre o abuelo tiene bastante de mito detrás, como demostró un médico que estuvo crujiéndose los nudillos durante muchos años para ver el efecto que tenía. Un médico alergólogo llamado Donald L. Unger estaba harto de escuchar estas advertencias durante su infancia y es por ello que optó por convertir su cuerpo en un laboratorio a largo plazo. item.description: Este jueves 29 de octubre, el fiscal antiterrorista de Francia, Olivier Christen, explicó que el autor del tiroteo –que mató a una persona e hirió a otras siete el pasado viernes– reconoció que el objetivo de sus disparos eran "musulmanes, africanos o norte-africanos". Las pesquisas han arrojado que el hombre de 39 años tuvo un "alto nivel de preparación" antes del ataque y que contaba en su vivienda con pegatinas de apoyo a la extrema derecha, aunque él aseguró no militar con ningún partido. item.description: Farming, dams and agricultural runoff are the biggest threats to freshwater biodiversity globally, with Europe and Northwest Africa the hardest-hit regions, McGill researchers have found. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Africa's water availability sometimes goes untapped
item.description: Water demand in Africa grew by around 26% between 2010 and 2020, yet around 717 million people lacked a piped water supply in 2020, according to research published in Nature. The findings indicate that water scarcity in some parts of Africa may be due to a lack of infrastructure, rather than a lack of available water. The work provides a comprehensive map for water demand in different sectors, highlighting issues that need to be addressed to increase the availability of water in Africa, which forms part of Sustainable Development Goal 6. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A 3,106-carat diamond pulled from a South African mine became the 530-carat gem in Britain's royal sceptre
item.description: Frederick Wells discovered the enormous Cullinan diamond in South Africa in 1905 while working at the Premier Mine. Its exceptional size caught public attention, leading to its purchase by the Transvaal government for King Edward VII. The diamond was carefully cut into several gemstones over eight months, resulting in noteworthy pieces for the British royal collection. Following Edward VII's death, the largest stone was incorporated into the Sovereign's Sceptre. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
